data.name: MIT Paper Shows Language Model Harnesses Boost Generalization
data.summary: A new MIT CSAIL paper by Alex L. Zhang, Souradip Chakraborty, and Omar Khattab argues that well-designed harnesses enable models to compose capabilities for stronger generalization on long or new tasks. By keeping prompts locally in-distribution through abstractions like context offloading and recursive sub-agent calls, these harnesses avoid errors from growing context windows in standard agents. Experiments on benchmarks like OOLONG and OBLiQ-Bench demonstrate models generalizing to tasks 8–64× longer, with gains like a 27B-parameter model improving 27% on long-context suites using fewer tokens. Co-authors stress that harness design and model learning are deeply intertwined, countering views that stronger models will make them obsolete.
